LESSON: PLANTS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Resources in Our Environment
Topic 3.2: Plants
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Plants, part of Resources in Our Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we care for plants in your environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify parts of a plant found in the school garden/ compound,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plants in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. draw different parts of a plant found at school,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plants in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. model different parts of a plant found at school,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plants in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. water plants found in their immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plants in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. show interest in parts of a plant for learning and enjoyment. ● Learners are guided to go for a nature walk in the school environment to collect young plants. Learners with blindness to be given one on one support during the walk. ● Learners with low vision use digital devices with assistive technology to watch video clips, observe pictures and photographs while learners with blindness listen to audio clips and picture description on different parts of a plant and identify them. ● Learners with low vision are guided to draw or take photographs of parts of a plant while learners with blindness are given tactile diagrams of parts of a plant found at school to manipulate and model. ● Learners are guided to plant seeds in the nature corner of the class, school garden or flowerbed. ● Learners are guided to water plants found in the immediate environment. ● In pairs or groups, learners display their work for further learning and peer assessment. How can we care for plants in your environment?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plants in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Plants together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner develops self-discipline as they go for a nature walk and explore different plants in the immediate environment.

Values:
Patriotism: learner enriches citizenship as they show love to their country by watering plants found in their immediate environment.

23

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Environmental Education and climate change: learner observes safety and responsibility when collecting young plants in the locality.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Plant relates to a concept of creation in Religious Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Approved learning support materials, digital devices with assistive technology, manilla papers, pictures, crayons, pencils, young plants

(uprooted), local environment.
